title: Hallucination in long-form factual generation
bottleneck: Models generate fluent, confident falsehoods — fabricated citations, invented facts, plausible nonsense — because training optimizes for likely text, not truth. No architecture enforces consistency between a model's claims and reality; retrieval grounding helps but models still misread sources, and long-form generation compounds errors. Hallucination rates on open-ended factual tasks remain far above what's acceptable for professional use.
why_it_blocks: Any application where truth matters — medicine, law, journalism, science — is blocked until outputs can be trusted without line-by-line human verification.
current_state: RAG and citation requirements reduce but don't eliminate hallucinations; production postmortems trace most hallucinations to unstable context rather than the model alone.
